scope: Learner-facing prose, decoded notation and source/attribution labels across all 14 Stage-E choices (gates Q10, Q15). Read-only against provider 0.1.4 (provider.py sha 0516286e…, calculus.py 44371979…, trig_log.py a1e56857…, visual.py 2f25b254…, catalogue-native.json 4004bc6f…).
method: Read checks/stage-e/wording.json, authoring/check_wording.py, checks/stage-e/notation.json, authoring/check_notation.mjs, math-expressions.json (6,028 items), playbook guidelines README + latex-generation-and-rendering + ui-language + ai-generated-output-formatting + shared-formatting-instruction snapshot, quality.md gate table/Q10/Q15, source/provider.py, source/provenance.json, catalogue-native.json examination_references, recipes.json public titles, OWNER-CHECKPOINT adaptation register.

Generated all 1,702 admitted domain instances with P.generate_at and learner_projection(mode='practice', reveal=True); also module.build for SVG bodies. Collected every learner-visible string: stem, practice_help title/prompts, part prompts, reference answers, worked-step action/reason/result, asset alt, must_read_givens, SVG <title>/<desc>/<text>/aria-label, examination learner_label -> 6,936 distinct strings (6,091 when restricted to the author's field set, matching wording.json). Script: work-wording/dump.py; data: work-wording/learner-strings.json.

Own copied-wording scan (work-wording/ngram.py): source corpus re-extracted with PyMuPDF directly from 430 PDFs = 10 NSSCAS 8227 papers 2021-2025 (all pages, incl. rubric/front pages), 5 full NSSCAS examiner reports, 415 Cambridge 9709 QPs/MSs (all cited in cambridge-evidence.json, catalogue, work-orders and planning). Two token modes: prose (maths stripped, like the author) and maths-normalised ($...$ converted to tokens: \sin->sin, \theta->theta, \text{} kept, digits kept, letters/digits split). Maximal-run 8-gram matcher. Result: prose 0 runs >=8; maths 1 distinct run >=12, 5 distinct runs of 8-11.

Supplementary character-level detector (work-wording/charmatch.py; whitespace/punctuation-free common substrings >=30 chars) over the same corpus: only standard rounding phrases, the R-form formula constraint and 'use a scalar product to find angle AOB'.

Supplementary corpus (work-wording/extra_sources.py): 119 NSSCAS award-table transcriptions (analysis/award-register-r4-draft.json, covers the raster mark-scheme tables) + 663-page OCR of the one textbook (analysis/ocr/ymxc). Prose 0 runs; maths runs only formula/coefficient coincidences (inspected).
Matcher sanity test: re-detected known source sentences (2023 P2 Q6(d) 25-word run; paper rubric 25-word run).

Notation: regex scans of all 6,936 strings for emphasis around maths, any Markdown emphasis, schema/transport ids, marking jargon, model/provider names, float reprs, unit-coefficient glitches, \prime, bare function names in maths, unpaired $, HTML, literal escapes, American spellings, claim/prediction words, punctuation glitches (work-wording/regex_scan.py, math_patterns.py, coef1b.py, punct.py).

Parsed every distinct learner string with the app's own micromark/mdast math+gfm parser (apps/web node_modules, read-only) and rendered all 6,028 distinct math nodes (11,208 occurrences) with app KaTeX 0.16.21 strict:'error', throwOnError:true (work-wording/render/parse_render.mjs -> render-check.json).

Visual render: 172 learner strings (>=10 per choice, >=7 distinct instances per choice; calculus 81, trig_log 52, visual 39 strings, each containing several expressions) rendered with app KaTeX under app options (strict:false, throwOnError:false) and app katex.min.css, screenshotted with local headless Chrome and inspected (render/gallery-*.png, crop-*.png); plus an 8-row side-by-side comparison (render/gallery-prime.png).

Labels: opened the cited PDF page for all 19 learner-displayed examination references (source sha256 re-hashed; printed page number read from page) and compared the source question/part with the bound generated part. Checked relation values, Cambridge/textbook/held-original display, and absence of exam-original tuples in 9 domains (work-wording/refpages.py, origcheck.py).
Claims/titles: regex for examiner/reward/prediction/guarantee/exam mentions over all learner strings; read all 14 recipe titles, 8 practice_help titles and prompts for answer cues.
Re-verified every should-fix instance against current bytes with fresh provider calls (work-wording/reverify.py -> reverify.json).

does: Scans stem, practice_help title+prompts, part prompt, reference_answer and every worked-step value for all 1,702 instances (6,091 distinct strings, confirmed equal to current bytes).

Compares lower-case alphabetic word 8-grams against analysis/extracted/*-questions.txt (question text of the 10 papers), report-*-mathematics.txt (text layer of the five report maths sections) and 30 Cambridge verbatim question transcriptions.
Flags claims only by regex 'examiners? (reward|require)|will (appear|come up)|guaranteed'.
does_not: Deletes every $...$ span and every numeral before tokenising, so formula-heavy copying is invisible (e.g. the R-form prompt reduces to 'express as where and give exactly and to two decimal places').
Omits asset alt text, must_read_givens, SVG text labels and examination learner labels.

Omits paper front/rubric pages and formula lists; omits NSSCAS mark schemes (award tables are raster images in the reports; transcriptions exist in award-register-r4-draft.json but are not used); omits all Cambridge mark schemes and full Cambridge papers (only 30 short question transcriptions); omits the textbook (OCR available).
Does not render or decode notation, check titles for cues, or cover runtime feedback (app-owned; none generated).
Claim regex misses 'in the exam', 'likely', 'predict', 'marks are awarded' etc. (my wider regex also found none).

findings.actual: 'Show that $y\prime=-\frac{2e^{2x}y}{e^{2x}+2y}$ where the denominator is nonzero, showing all necessary working.' findings.expected: Runs of 12+ identical words repaired unless a documented formula/standard exception is accepted.
findings.actual: 'Express $\sin\theta+2\cos\theta$ as $R\sin(\theta+\alpha)$, where $R>0$ and $0^\circ<\alpha<90^\circ$. Give …' shares a 12-token maths-normalised run 'R sin θ α where R 0 and 0 α 90 Give' with NSSCAS 2022 P2 Q6(a) p8 ('in the form R sin(θ + α), where R > 0 and 0° < α < 90°. Give the value of α…'). Only 3 prose words (where/and/give); the rest is the standard R-form constraint, which appears verbatim in >=8 Cambridge 9709 papers (w15_qp_21 p2, s19_qp_22 p10, s22_qp_22 p12, m21_qp_32 p8 …; their θ/α glyphs extract as '1'/'!' so the matcher under-counts them). Recommend recording it as an allowed formula exception; no rewording needed.

findings.criterion: Q15 8-11 word runs for manual judgement
findings.actual: (1) vector b prompt (30/30) 'Use a scalar product to find angle $AOB$ …' = 8-word verbatim command from the cited NSSCAS 2025 P1 Q3(b) p5 and Cambridge 9709 w16_qp_12/s17_qp_12 — necessary command terminology, allowed. (2) graph-intercept stem (270/270) 'The variables satisfy $y=Ae^{px+p}$, where $A>0$. The graph of $\ln y$ against $x$ is shown.' — 8-token run 'the graph of ln y against x is' (NSSCAS 2023 P2 Q4(a) p6, Cambridge s15_qp_21, s22_qp_21) and the whole stem closely paraphrases 2023 P2 Q4(a) ('The variables x and y satisfy the equation y = Ae^{px+p}, where A and p are constants. The graph of ln y against x is a straight line…'); standard terminology + same-type model, allowed but worth recording. (3) vector stem 'the position vectors of A, B and C' (8; NSSCAS 2025 P1 Q3 + Cambridge) — standard. (4) two-extrema stems 'For the function f(x)=x³−3x²−9x+…' / '…−24x+…' share 9-12 tokens with Cambridge w16_qp_13 and textbook p288 — coefficient coincidence (signs/constants differ), not copying. (5) numeric coincidences ('2 2 3 3 2 2 2 2', 't³+½t²+2t' vs award 2021-1-Q4 where source has t³) — not copying. No prose run >=8 against papers, reports, award tables, Cambridge QP/MS or textbook OCR.
